name: Coelho and Vespucci along Brazil
summary: A small fleet sent to see what Cabral had found sails some three thousand kilometres along the coast of Brazil, naming its capes and bays for the saints' days on which they reach them: All Saints' Bay, the River of January. Aboard is the Florentine Amerigo Vespucci, whose letter Mundus Novus told Europe that this was not Asia but a new world, and a German mapmaker put his name on it.

stops.note: They meet Cabral's fleet coming home from India.
Landfall at the north-eastern shoulder of Brazil.
Named for the day they enter it, 1 November.
A great bay they take for a river's mouth: the River of January.
Home with brazilwood and the outline of a continent.

informs.note: Three thousand kilometres of the coast charted
